label: Capture
blurb: What starts a read, and how much of the screen it looks at.

fields.label: Trigger
fields.help: 'key' reads when you press the key. 'auto' reads on a timer.

fields.label: Read key
fields.help: Full-screen read. A single character, or a name like f9.

fields.label: Focused read key
fields.help: Reads a box around the centre of the screen, more thoroughly. Use it when a name sits just above your crosshair.

fields.label: Chat read key
fields.help: Reads the chat window and lists everyone talking. Chat handles are crisp UI text with the original capitalisation, so they are more reliable than a HUD label - measured on the reference frame, four of four resolved to real accounts. 'off' disables it.

fields.label: Chat window region
fields.help: 'auto' works it out from your resolution, which is right unless you have dragged the chat window somewhere else - and looks in both places the game puts it: with your helmet on (a pitch indicator pushes chat to the right) and with it off. A region you set is read as it is, so it has to cover wherever you use chat. Chat sits a fixed distance left of screen CENTRE, so a fixed fraction of the width - what this used to be - framed the chat on a 3440 or 5120 screen and missed it entirely on a 2560 one. To override, give x,y,width,height as fractions of the screen, e.g. 0.15,0.30,0.35,0.45. Chat grows upward as messages arrive, so a region covering only the newest line reads one name instead of five.

fields.label: Wide + centre key
fields.help: Reads the whole screen AND the centre on one press, then merges them. The centre reading wins where they overlap, because it had the whole budget to itself. Measured at about 1.4x the time of a normal read, and on displays where the normal read struggles it found several times as many contacts. Worth trying if you are missing people. 'off' disables it.

fields.label: Make the normal read key do both
fields.help: Turns every normal read into a wide + centre read, without needing a second binding. Simpler than a separate key, and you pay the doubled cost on every ping.

fields.label: Focused box size
fields.help: 'auto' sizes the box from your resolution: the measured 1200x600 scaled by screen height, because the HUD scales with vertical resolution and that figure was tuned on a 1440-tall screen. At 1080p it becomes 900x450, at 4K 1800x900. Override with pixels, width x height, centred on the crosshair - e.g. 1200x600.

fields.label: Mask focused reads
fields.help: Run the brightness mask on focused reads instead of sending the crop straight to OCR. Slower, and only occasionally better.

fields.label: Frames per read
fields.help: More frames means more chances to agree on a name, and a longer wait for the last word.

fields.label: Gap between frames
fields.help: How long to wait between the frames of one read. Tight is better: contacts drift and labels fade, and a late frame often catches neither. Try 0.1 first. Above about 0.5 the hit rate drops off, so treat that as the practical ceiling rather than the range end.

fields.label: Delay before first frame
fields.help: Waits after the key press before grabbing, to let a scan animation finish. Every second cut here is a second off your answer.

fields.label: Always-on read delay
fields.help: With Trigger 'auto': how long to wait after a new contact appears before reading it. The HUD types a new name in letter by letter, and reading at once caught half-typed names (looked up, not found, never merged). Measured: the whole name was there 0.3 s after a half-typed frame.

fields.label: Monitor
fields.help: 1-based index of the screen the game is on.

fields.label: HDR capture
fields.help: With Windows HDR on for the game's screen, the ordinary screen copy treats 80 nits as white: the picture arrives blown out and HUD text sits in a white halo, so names are misread. 'auto' captures the HDR picture itself and converts it back to the game's own image (about 40 ms of CPU a frame at 5120x1440) - what makes NVIDIA RTX HDR, which needs Windows HDR on, work with sc-watch. 'off' always uses the ordinary copy. Star Citizen's own HDR option should stay off either way: it makes HUD text bloom in the game itself.

fields.label: Key poll rate
fields.help: How often the trigger key is checked.

fields.label: Queued reads
fields.help: How many key presses may stack up while a read is already running.

label: Detection
blurb: How hard the reader tries, and what it is willing to believe.

fields.label: Name reader
fields.help: Who finds and reads the name plates. 'iris' (the default) is IRIS's finder and per-letter reader, ported from github.com/Niteb1rd/IRIS (GPL-3.0): about ten times faster than OCR (0.11 s a frame against 1.2 s). Focused reads are off with it - they exist to work around OCR's limits - so the focus and dual keys do a full read. 'iris+ocr' adds OCR for the plates IRIS is unsure of (at most 4 a frame) and keeps focused reads on OCR. 'ocr' is sc-watch's own pipeline from before 0.3.0: slower, but in a busy cockpit - the heading tape, pitch ladder and labels crowding a plate - it finds plates IRIS's finder skips. IRIS needs clean HUD text: keep Star Citizen's own HDR option off (its glow joins the letters). Chat reads use OCR whatever this says: IRIS reads name plates only.

fields.label: IRIS scan area
fields.help: With an IRIS reader ('iris+ocr' or 'iris'): how much of the screen is searched. 'whole' misses nothing; 'narrow' skips 5% top and bottom and 3% each side; 'iris' is IRIS's own default, 15% and 8%, which skips contacts near the edges; 'centre' searches the middle half. Smaller is faster.

fields.label: IRIS always-on scan area
fields.help: With an IRIS reader and Trigger 'auto': the area searched on every frame to notice a new contact (reads still use the scan area above). It runs continuously, so it defaults to 'narrow'.

fields.label: OpenCV threads
fields.help: How many CPU threads OpenCV's image work may use (IRIS's scan is almost all OpenCV). Measured in game, always-on with the IRIS reader: 2 threads used half the CPU of OpenCV's default (1.6-1.7 cores down to 0.8) at the same scan speed - with the game running, the extra threads only compete with it for cores. 0 = OpenCV's default, every core.

fields.label: Votes to announce
fields.help: How many frames of a burst must agree before a name is said out loud. 1 announces fast and is sometimes wrong.

fields.label: Range gate
fields.help: Require a range line to look like a range before trusting the pair.

fields.label: Re-read dim range lines
fields.help: Turn this on if you can plainly see contact names that are never reported. On some displays the range line under a name renders dimmer than the name, so the name is found and the contact is thrown away for having no range. This re-reads the strip underneath. It costs roughly 1.5s per read and finds nothing at all on a display that does not have the problem, which is why it is off by default.

fields.label: Haze locator
fields.help: Adds a fourth, brighter locator pass. Helps against a bright planet surface; finds more junk in space.

fields.label: Re-announce after
fields.help: Too short and a wingman re-announces all session; too long and you miss a genuine return.

fields.label: Pairing radius
fields.help: How far below a name its range line may sit.

fields.label: Contact expiry
fields.help: How long a contact stays 'current' after its last sighting.

label: Audio
blurb: What you hear when something is found.

fields.label: Audio
fields.help: Tones are fast and unambiguous; speech tells you the name.

fields.label: Speech rate
fields.help: Words per minute.

fields.label: Say handles aloud
fields.help: Off gives you the warning without the name.

fields.label: Handles spoken per read
fields.help: A crowded screen otherwise talks over the fight.

fields.label: Summarise above
fields.help: More contacts than this and you get a count instead of names.

label: RSI lookups
blurb: When to ask the API who a handle belongs to.

fields.label: Look handles up
fields.help: Fetches org and enlistment data for handles it reads.

fields.label: Lookup source
fields.help: 'sentry' asks SENTRY first - fast, no key needed, it sees every org a player is in, and it gives each org's focus - then starcitizen-api.com for anything SENTRY cannot answer. 'sci' uses only starcitizen-api.com, the way it worked before SENTRY. An account is only taken as NOT existing when RSI was asked - by starcitizen-api.com, or by SENTRY checking it - never because a database has not heard of it.

fields.label: Votes before lookup
fields.help: A misread handle wastes a request and pollutes the database, so weak reads are not looked up automatically. Confirming an audit by hand always looks up, whatever this says.

fields.label: API mode
fields.help: 'auto' uses the cache where it can. 'live' is always fresh and slower. Org rosters force 'live' regardless.

label: Shared watchlists
blurb: Lists other people keep. Their claims, shown as theirs - never folded into your own records and never counted in your score.

fields.label: Use shared watchlists
fields.help: Flags a contact when a list you have imported names them, showing whose list it was and what they said. Off hides every source at once without deleting anything - the import is still there when you turn it back on.

fields.label: Flag lookalike spellings
fields.help: Also flags a handle that could be an OCR misreading of a listed name - SLIVER against 5LIVER. Shown as 'a name like this is on…' and never raises an alert on its own, because those are two different real people. Off means exact matches only.

label: Audit
blurb: Keeping the picture behind a read, so you can check it by eye.

fields.label: Write a session log
fields.help: A text log in debug_bursts/ recording your settings and what the watcher read from every frame. A few KB per session and the last 12 are kept. Separate from 'Save every frame (debug)' ON PURPOSE: the frames cost 4.7 MB each so they are opt-in, but a log that only starts once you turn it on misses the thing you were about to report. Secrets are redacted - see 'Make a support bundle' under Storage & cleanup.

fields.label: Save uncertain reads
fields.help: When a read is not corroborated, keep the crops that produced it.

fields.label: Keep audits for
fields.help: Unreviewed audits older than this are deleted along with their images. Confirming or dismissing one deletes it immediately.

fields.label: Keep the full frame
fields.help: The whole screen, not just the crops, so you can see what the contact actually was. Around 0.6 MB each.

fields.label: Frame quality
fields.help: JPEG quality for that full frame. Lower is smaller.

label: Storage & cleanup
blurb: Captured frames are big. This is what stops them piling up.

fields.label: Save every frame (debug)
fields.help: Writes every burst frame to debug_bursts/ so a missed contact can be diagnosed afterwards. Around 4.7 MB per frame - this is the setting that fills a disk.

fields.label: Delete old frames
fields.help: Master switch for the cleanup below.

fields.label: Clean up at startup
fields.help: Run a sweep when the watcher starts.

fields.label: Clean up every
fields.help: Time between sweeps while the watcher runs. 0 means only at startup.

fields.label: Always keep newest
fields.help: Never delete below this many per directory, however old.

fields.label: Hard file cap
fields.help: Per directory, whatever the age. 0 turns the cap off. Useful when a long session would fill the disk before the age rule ever applies.

fields.label: Contacts shown
fields.help: How many of the most recent contacts the grid draws. Measured cost is about 0.2 ms per tile to render and 0.4 ms to assemble, and only when the data actually changes - so this is a readability control, not a performance one. Lower it if the board is too busy to scan.

fields.label: Tile size
fields.help: Minimum width of a contact tile. The grid fits as many as will go, so a bigger number means fewer, larger tiles - at 2560 wide, 380 gives six across and 500 gives four. Text scales with the tile.

fields.label: Square tiles
fields.help: Keeps every tile the same shape so rows line up. Tiles still grow taller when a contact has more to show.

fields.label: Show advanced settings
fields.help: Reveals the settings that are easiest to get wrong.
